We can see, I think, there an entry crossed out and a little later another entry, which is dated 21 September. Is that an entry that you recognise or is that after you finished your shift?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: No, that's my...
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It's just a little bit difficult to make out.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: No, I think that is my signature there with Yvonne Farmer on the second line down.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We can see the date it started.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Not so easy to make out the time. Do you happen to recall what time that started?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: No. I've said in my patient notes, though, that I commenced it.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Sorry, commenced that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: I don't know. I said in my patient notes that I had commenced it, but (overspeaking) --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Without a specific time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: -- which we looked at earlier.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Do you happen to recall whether that was after [Baby G] had been moved to room 1?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: It was, yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: All right. We looked at some of the management staff that were on duty on the ward, albeit not at that time with clinical responsibilities. Did you speak to any of the management about what had happened or what you'd seen that afternoon?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: I did, yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Who did you speak to?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: I spoke to the shift leader, Caroline Bennion, and the ward manager, Eirian Powell.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think about a month ago, you contacted the police to tell them about another conversation you had that afternoon on the ward; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And it was to do, I think, with you finding the monitor switched off when you came to -- when you responded initially to Lucy Letby's call for help; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I didn't ask you this and I should have: when it was switched off, could you actually see whether it had been physically switched off? Would you see the on/off button at all?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: So it was a black screen, which means it's off. Yes, it was off.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Who was that other conversation that you remembered last month with? The more recent conversation.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: As in who...?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Who was the conversation with.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Who I've reported it to?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: DC Millins.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Right. What was it you told DC Millins?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: I told her that I had read the opening speeches online and it suggested that Lucy had switched off the monitor --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: -- whereas I knew that not to be -- well, as far as I know, not to be the case.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. As far as you know, how is that so?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Because Dr Gibbs and Dr Harkness told me after the event that they were very sorry that they'd left [Baby G] behind the screen, that they hadn't moved the screen away, and that they'd left her without a monitor.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. How did that conversation come about?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Eirian must have spoken to them or they've gone to Eirian and told her that's what's happened because I've gone to Eirian and told her that the monitor's off -- I didn't know at that time how or why it was off because it's not normal protocol.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: All right. So it obviously stood out to you, so you told Eirian that the monitor had been switched off?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Do I understand it right that you understand that it was Eirian to whom Dr Gibbs and Dr Harkness spoke?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: I don't know what conversations they had with each other. I know I went to Eirian and Caroline Bennion, the shift leader, and I told them that when the shout for help came the response appeared normal but the monitor was switched off.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. I just want to clarify, I'm sorry. Did you speak directly with Doctors Harkness and Gibbs about it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes, I did.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. Putting aside what others may have been told or what others may have told you, can you remember exactly the conversation you had with Doctors Harkness and Gibbs?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: No one has said anything to me about it and I have not discussed it with anyone.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, no, I mean that afternoon.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: That afternoon they came to me, very, very apologetic, very concerned that the screen had been left in situ and they hadn't come to tell me that they had finished with the care with [Baby G] at that time --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: -- and they had not switched the monitor back on.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So this was a conversation directly with you?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes, 100%.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And do you remember where it took place?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes, in the corridor just outside nursery 4.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. Can you remember how long after the incident this conversation took place?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: During that afternoon.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Was it immediately after, was it after you'd been to Eirian and told Eirian what you were concerned about?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Was it before that? Can you put it in the timeline anywhere?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: No, I'm sorry, I can't.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. Again, if you can't help, please tell us, was it still daylight when you had the conversation? It was September so it might help where it was in your shift.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Well, it was during managerial working hours, put it that way, which end at no later than 6.00.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. So some point before 6 o'clock, but obviously after the event?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: After the event, yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And forgive me, just before or after you'd spoken to Eirian, are you able to say?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: I don't know.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: All right. Was it both of the doctors who said it or just one of the doctors?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: They were both present. I don't know who said it.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. So one said it in the presence of the other?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: They both might have said it, I don't know. I just know I was with them and one or both told me that it happened.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay, all right. And you first remembered this conversation when you read the opening from the trial; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: I'd remembered it all the way through.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: When I read it in the opening speeches, I asked DC Millins if I could review my statement and listen to my transcript, which I hadn't previously done so, because I believed that I had already said that during the original statement.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The jury have heard this before, but the process for taking your statement was that you were recorded -- audio recorded by the police.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: In some detail, was that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Then a witness statement provided from that recording?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Which you were then given the opportunity to read, check, and sign if you were content with it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Correct.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And again, just so I understand, the information that you gave DC Millins about a month or so ago, was that in the recording or the statement?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: The conversation was not in the transcript, but the detective that interviewed me asked me, "Is this normal procedure?", and I've said no. And he's -- I can't remember now, but it's in the transcript, which is available, I've seen it this morning. I have said that is for Dr Gibbs and Dr Harkness to comment, but obviously 4 years have passed but I thought I'd told the conversation but I hadn't.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: You have checked the transcript, it's not actually in there, but you have told us what is in the transcript on that subject?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes, I've told them, I've told the detective: you need to ask them, I wasn't present for whatever went on with that monitor, you need to ask them themselves what happened.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Blood gas good this evening. Will repeat in 4 hours with blood sugar as 9mmols."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: 9 millimoles, yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: The second one, yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: NURSE B: Well, just based on this one, to repeat in 4 hours the blood gas with the blood sugar, and then, after the next one, they would determine when the one after would be.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Thank you. Then I think there's one final addendum to your notes if we go to tile 90. It might be the same addendum, let's just check. Yes. I think it reappears because it was actually entered on the computer at 18.39. Thank you.

blocks.text: I have no more questions, but if you could wait there, please.
